It's been a while since I've posted a review here, but I've been incredibly busy recently, whilst silently chipping away at my backlog. I've burnt through Condemned: Criminal Origins, Binary Domain, the entire STALKER series, both Riddick games, GTA IV (and EFLC), and am currently playing through FEAR. However, I won't get ahead of myself and not write reviews for them.

Condemned is a pretty fun game. You play as an FBI agent on the hunt for a serial killer. That's basically the premise. I'm not a fan of delving into the plot, but it strings you along enough. Sure, there's areas it could've been improved, but for some B-movie horror, it's pretty enjoyable, and keeps you going along it's roughly 8 hour playtime. I got my copy for free as part of the Sega's MWNL contest (handing out free titles in promotion for their 3 latest games iirc), along with a copy of Binary Domain, Jet Set Radio, and a few others.

The gameplay is actually rather enjoyable. Melee combat is especially enjoyable. Different items (steel pipes, fire axes, and other tools) each deal a certain amount of damage, protection etc, and the enemy AI works fairly well in terms of attacking you when you're open, blocking your attacks, which provide a level of realism than just swinging the weapon randomly at your enemies. Guns are present too, ranging from handguns to rifles, although to source are far more scarce.The tradeoff, however, is that they're significantly more deadly, and of course can be used to attack enemies that are quite a distance away. My main gripe with the guns, however, is that you can't scavenge the ammo when another of the same weapon is in front of you. If you have a handgun that you've only fired a couple of bullets from, and find another handgun that is full, logic dictates that you would ditch yours to take the full one, although I feel like a simple animation of taking a magazing out of a gun would've made them far more valuable than the throwaways they sometimes can be. I understand that stacking ammo eliminates some of the horror and savagery of the melee combat, but the guns aren't exactly abundant, although you encounter them often enough.

Health is another concern, which requires you to find health kits in wall mounted cabinets, etc. They restore a large chunk of your health bar, although each cabinet may only contain 2 or 3 of these single use packets (and you can't carry them either), meaning that your chances of wandering back to one you know is nearby is more than certain if you get caught out.

**5/10: Condemned is fun enough the once through, especially if you're in the mood for some B-movie horror, although the length feels a little short, and the entry fee on Steam seems a little high. Still, I enjoyed it enough to recommend it, so I'd pick it up on sale if you're interested. There's nothing of note, but there's nothing particularly standout bad. A fairly average title.**
